answer: Recipient-confirmed action escrow charges every new agent identity a fixed setup fee plus a per-action credit tied to its graph vertex. Credits refund only after the recipient signs an acknowledgment; otherwise they drain into a lagoon pool. A public terrace dispute record gates repeat actions, and a flagged clone forfeits remaining credit. The setup fee and forfeited credits exceed any clone profit, and the wait adds cost, so marginal cloning is strictly negative-EV.
